title: Report verb-object naming drift across the existing wagon/feature corpus without blocking

facts.note: Source validation.phase is CONFIRM; the scan runs on every CONFIRM regardless of task wording or prior findings. The planning phase is not currently exposed as an observable fact.

Subject is the authored wagon/feature corpus already on disk (validation.subject_kind wagon; statement covers wagon and feature names), not session.kept_units(). No current observer enumerates the on-disk corpus; one is needed.

fires: Every CONFIRM run: scan the existing wagon and feature names on disk and report the non-conforming count, including when the count is zero and when every artifact was authored through the plan session.

Interpreting a drift report (separate from running the check): the planner reads the count and decides whether a rise signals new out-of-gate drift, or is tempted to widen the lexicon or block on a non-zero count.
doesNotFire: Naming a new wagon or feature inside a plan session — that authoring path is gated by planner.wagon.name-is-verb-object / planner.feature.name-is-verb-object, not by this report.

given: A CONFIRM run with wagon and feature artifacts on disk (whatever their history or conformance)
when: The corpus naming check scans those names, or the planner reads its drift report
then: Report every non-conforming wagon/feature name (artifact kind, slug, reason) with a total count, as advisory only — never block on it.
prefer: Treat the count as the signal: a rising count means new drift entered outside the authoring gate — the only actionable part; a falling count means debt was paid opportunistically.
avoid: Widening the verb lexicon to clear the report — it silences a rule that correctly describes the corpus.
Turning the report into a blocking gate or failing a plan because the count is non-zero.
why: Authoring gates read only the session's kept units, so hand-renamed or out-of-session artifacts drift unnoticed; the count makes drift visible. It stays advisory because renaming is unaffordable, and a blocking rule with no affordable remedy gets ignored.
evidence: The corpus check output lists each non-conforming wagon/feature with artifact_kind, slug and reason, plus a total count (also reported when zero).
The check runs with advisory enforcement (severity 2): non-conforming names never fail the run.
The lexicon was not widened to lower the count; a rise versus the previous count is surfaced as new out-of-gate drift.
verifier_detail: Validator: family=format, template=naming_pattern, variant=planner_artifact_naming_verb_object_corpus_drift, phase=CONFIRM, enforcement=advisory, subject_kind=wagon (wagon and feature names on disk are scanned).
failure_evidence fields per finding: artifact_kind, slug, reason.
Disposition advisory, severity 2: report with count, never block; the disposition is load-bearing by design.

Scans the corpus on disk, NOT session.kept_units(). planner.wagon.name-is-verb-object and planner.feature.name-is-verb-object gate the authoring path (confirm_naming reads session.kept_units(), so anything authored through atdd plan conforms by construction); neither looks at the corpus. This rule is the corpus half.
Typical non-conformance reasons observed: name leads with a noun; name carries an `and` connective; (rarely) leading verb genuinely missing from the lexicon.

Count semantics: the count is the artefact. Rising = new drift entered outside the authoring gate (the only actionable signal); falling = debt paid opportunistically, while someone was already touching the artifact for other reasons.

Rename cost (why non-blocking): a name is carried by the directory, the wagon URN, every feature/WMBT/acceptance URN beneath it, test filenames, component URNs in code headers, both registries and the State Store bindings — renaming one wagon touches roughly 54 files, 37 of them tests.
audit: schema_version 1.0.0; source kind: policy; status: active.
Source name: 'Verb-object drift across the authored corpus is reported'.
Term ids: corpus_not_gate, reports_never_blocks, drift_is_the_signal, not_a_lexicon_gap.

Baseline measurement at authoring time: 101 of 229 authored artifacts did not conform. Of the 101, 92 led with a noun (coach x11, substrate x4, phase x3, pr x3) and 9 carried an `and` connective; only 2 verbs were genuinely missing from the lexicon.

Rename cost measured: renaming one wagon touches roughly 54 files, 37 of them tests (directory, wagon URN, feature/WMBT/acceptance URNs, test filenames, component URNs in code headers, both registries, State Store bindings).

additions.justification: Schema requires concrete activation situations; derived from the source's CONFIRM phase, corpus-vs-authoring split and count interpretation. No new obligation.

additions.text: Count reported even when zero; rise compared against the previous count
additions.justification: Operationalises the source's 'report with a count' and 'rising count is the actionable signal' so a reviewer can verify them; no new obligation on the planner.
